NUTRITION PLAN FOR INSULIN SENSITIVITY
  GOALS
    - Support insulin sensitivity and metabolic health
    - Preserve lean mass and avoid under-fuelling
    - Provide consistent energy for training and daily activity

  GUIDING PRINCIPLES
    - Calorie: moderate energy balance with small surplus on heavy training days or maintenance on rest days to support recovery and weight stability.
    - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day to maintain/optimise lean mass and satiety.
    - Carbohydrates: focus on low glycemic index sources, distributed evenly across 3–4 meals around training; target 3–5 g/kg/day total depending on activity.
    - Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day from mostly unsaturated sources; emphasize omega-3 intake.
    - Fiber: 25–38 g/day from diverse plant sources.
    - Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day minimum; adjust for activity and climate.
    - Timing: protein and carbs around workouts; post-workout protein within 1–2 hours.

  DAILY STRUCTURE (example target ranges)
    - Calorie target: maintain current body weight with slight surplus on higher-intensity days; adjust weekly by ±150–250 kcal if weight drift observed.
    - Protein: 1.8 g/kg/day average.
    - Carbohydrates: 3.5–5.0 g/kg/day on training days, 2.5–3.5 g/kg/day on rest days.
    - Fats: 0.9–1.0 g/kg/day.

  SAMPLE MACROS (for a 70 kg reference)
    - Training days: ~210 g protein, 350–420 g carbohydrates, 60–70 g fats, total ~2600–2900 kcal.
    - Rest days: ~210 g protein, 240–320 g carbohydrates, 60–70 g fats, total ~2100–2300 kcal.

  NUTRIENT STRATEGIES
    - Protein distribution: 4 meals with 40–50 g protein each, or 3 meals with 50–60 g protein plus 1 snack with 20–30 g as needed.
    - Fiber-rich vegetables: include at least 2–3 cups per day; diversify colors.
    - Sleep hygiene: aim 7–9 hours; supports insulin sensitivity.
    - Sodium: moderate; avoid excessive ultra-processed foods.

  MEAL PLAN ELEMENTS (per day)
    - Lean protein: chicken, turkey, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes.
    - Whole grains: oats, quinoa, brown rice, barley.
    - Legumes and veggies: beans, lentils, cruciferous and leafy greens.
    - Fruits: berries, apples, citrus in moderation.
    - Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds; emphasize fatty fish a couple times weekly.
    - Hydration: water; limit sugar-sweetened beverages.

  WEEKLY ADJUSTMENTS
    - Track weight, energy, and training performance.
    - If weight increases >0.5 kg/week, reduce total calories by 150–200 kcal on non-training days and maintain protein.
    - If energy visibly low, consider small lift in calories (100–150 kcal) and/or adjust carbohydrate around workouts.

  SUPPLEMENT CONSIDERATIONS (optional, after clinician guidance)
    - Vitamin D if deficient; magnesium if deficient or for sleep support.
    - Omega-3 fatty acids (1–3 g/day) from fish oil or algae sources.
    - Consider a micronutrient-rich multivitamin to cover gaps.

  SAFETY AND MONITORING
    - No extreme caloric restrictions; avoid under-fuelling as it worsens insulin sensitivity and PCOS symptoms.
    - Monitor satiety, energy levels, menstrual health, and mood.
    - If any adverse symptoms arise, consult healthcare provider.

RECOVERY FRAMEWORK
  1) Flare recognition and early action
     - If new or worsening back pain, fatigue, or systemic symptoms occur, treat as a potential flare.
     - Apply "start with safer, lower-load work" rule: reduce intensity by 20–40%, reduce volume by 20–40%, and shorten sessions to 30–45 minutes when needed.
     - Allow 2–5 days of low-load activity (e.g., walking, gentle mobility) before reassessing.
     - Use pain and functional checks: pain at or above 4/10 during basic movements warrants regression or pause.

  2) Session structure during flare
     - Warmup: 5–10 minutes of light cardio and mobility; avoid spinal loading.
     - Main: 1–2 sets per exercise at low RPE (5–6), 6–8 reps, 60–90 seconds rest; prioritize movements that do not aggravate symptoms.
     - Choice of exercises: favor horizontal pushes/pulls, goblet squats, assisted variations, glute bridges, light core stabilization (pain-free).
     - Volume cap: limit total sets to 6–12 in a session; total workload should stay well below pre-flare baseline.

  3) Post-flare reassessment and progression
     - After 2–7 days of improved symptoms, reintroduce progression gradually:
       - Step back up to near-baseline volume over 1–2 weeks.
       - Increase load by small increments (2–5%) or add one additional set every 1–2 weeks if pain-free.
     - If symptoms persist beyond 7–14 days or worsen, pause resistance training characteristics and seek medical guidance.

  4) Cycle-irregularity considerations
     - Do not anchor progression to cycle phase; instead, treat each week by current symptom status.
     - If fatigue, sleep disruption, or mood changes occur (common in PCOS), consider a temporary reduction in weekly total volume or intensity.
     - Maintain protein intake and overall caloric adequacy to support metabolic health even during lighter weeks.

     - Use a simple daily log: pain score, sleep duration, energy, and training load (RPE and sets/reps).
     - Track any changes in bowel/bladder or neurological symptoms; escalate if red flags arise.

     - If back pain is persistent, sharp, numbness, or radiating, halt resistance training and consult clinician.

     - Return-to-training resume only when pain-free or with clear medical clearance.
